findings.title: refundFlow namespace (261/264 keys) is English-only in de/fr/it, with a live _todo_translate marker ignored for 7+ weeks
findings.principle: Any namespace containing a boolean or non-string sentinel key (e.g. `_todo_translate: true`) fails CI immediately: a pre-merge script scans every messages/*.json for non-string leaf values and non-en locale files whose string value is byte-identical to the en.json value at the same key, and blocks merge until the count is zero or the key is added to a named, dated allowlist. A namespace may not ship customer-facing (i.e. reachable outside /dev) until every locale's translator-facing string differs from the English placeholder or is explicitly allowlisted with an owner-approved reason.
findings.why: A TODO marker that lives only as data (a JSON key) with no code path that reads it and fails is invisible to every existing gate (typecheck, lint, invariants) and to the human eye unless someone opens the raw JSON. The result is a fully shipped, customer-reachable feature (dispute/refund reporting, entryDeskTitle: 'Report a problem or request a refund') that has been silently English-only for German, French, and Italian users for the entire time it has existed, which would read as broken or untrustworthy on a page whose entire purpose is trust recovery.
findings.local_evidence: messages/de.json line 6114 has a literal `"_todo_translate": true` inside the `refundFlow` object. Programmatic flatten of all four locale files shows refundFlow has 264 keys in de/fr/it and 263 in en (the extra is the marker itself); of those, 261 of 264 keys in de, fr, AND it are byte-identical to the English string (e.g. refundFlow.upTitle = 'Approve an extra charge' in all four files). `git log -S "_todo_translate" --format="%ad %h %s" -- messages/de.json` shows it was introduced 2026-06-02 ('feat: refund/dispute hardening') and last touched 2026-06-13 in an i18n sweep commit that fixed other strings but left this namespace untouched; today is 2026-07-26, so it has sat live and un-swept for roughly 7-8 weeks.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri "_todo_translate\|todo.translate\|sentinel key\|non-string message" _design-system _rules _docs CLAUDE.md _backend-system ~/.claude/*.md ~/.claude/hooks -> zero hits anywhere. No script in package.json or .github/workflows/*.yml reads messages/*.json for non-string values or cross-locale identity.
findings.existing_coverage: none. I18N_ROUTING.md Rule 37 says new feature copy 'must be treated as a placeholder... add to de.json, en.json, fr.json, it.json' but has no check that the added value is an actual translation rather than an English copy-paste, and no check for stray non-string keys.
findings.where_it_should_live: _rules/I18N_ROUTING.md (new Rule 40) + a new scripts/check-i18n-parity.mjs wired into .github/workflows/quality.yml
findings.enforcement: gate: ci-i18n-parity (new script, blocks merge on non-string leaf keys or new identical-to-en strings outside an allowlist)

findings.title: German 'du not Sie' is locked law but has zero enforcement and is already violated 12 times in the live de.json, including inside dashboard chrome
findings.principle: The locked German register (SOURCE.md section 18/20: 'du not Sie') is enforced the same way the existing copy-lint-gate enforces no-caps and no-em-dash: a PreToolUse regex gate blocks any Write/Edit to messages/de.json (or a de-locale literal in a .tsx file) that introduces a formal-register token (Ihr, Ihre, Ihren, Ihrer, Ihnen, Sie as a pronoun) outside an explicit allowlisted namespace (legal.*, *_tos.*, and any key an owner has named as intentionally formal). A pre-existing violation must be fixed or allowlisted in the same commit that touches its file, not left to accumulate.
findings.why: A style rule that lives only in a markdown table has no mechanism to catch drift once the corpus is 5600+ keys deep and edited by many independent turns; without a grep-backed gate, formal register creeps back in exactly where a copy-paste from a legal/formal template is easiest, i.e. transactional or verification-flow copy, and nobody notices because the rest of the screen still reads informally.
findings.local_evidence: Programmatic scan of messages/de.json: 196 informal tokens (dein/deine/deinem/deiner/dir/dich) vs 12 formal tokens (Ihre/Ihren/Ihnen). Of those 12, most are correctly confined to legal.privacy.* and discovery_tos.* (expected, since legal documents conventionally stay formal even in an informal-voice product) but 5 are NOT: dashboard.settings.quickReplyDefault1 ('Vielen Dank fur Ihre Nachricht!'), dashboard.settings.quickReplyDefault2 ('Ihr Termin wurde bestatigt.'), dashboard.settings.closuresIntro ('...an denen Ihr Salon geschlossen ist'), dashboard.disputes.responsePlaceholder ('Ihre Stellungnahme zum Vorfall...'), dashboard.verificationPage.yourDocuments ('Ihre Dokumente'), and dashboard.messagesPage.quickReplyThanks/quickReplyConfirmed (duplicates of the settings ones). These sit in the SAME dashboard.settings namespace that elsewhere uses 'dein/deine' 15+ times (e.g. dashboard.settings.vatNumberHint: 'Deine Schweizer Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer'), so this is drift within one namespace, not a deliberate split.
findings.absence_proof: SOURCE.md section 18 states 'Conversational - German du not Sie (per audience research)' and section 20's locked-decisions table repeats 'German du not Sie / (since launch)'; both are prose-only. grep -rn "Sie-form\|no-sie-gate\|register-gate\|formal-register" ~/.claude/hooks and .claude/hooks -> zero hits. copy-lint-gate.py (the file that DOES enforce no-caps/no-emdash/no-separator/no-verbose-copy as a merged PreToolUse hook) has no fifth rule for register.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: SOURCE.md section 18 + section 20 state the rule as law but supply no detection mechanism and no rule for WHICH namespaces are legitimately exempt (legal vs. product chrome), so a reviewer has no fast way to tell an intentional legal-formal string from drift.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md section 18 (add the allowlist) + a fifth check appended to ~/.claude/hooks/copy-lint-gate.py
findings.enforcement: gate: extend copy-lint-gate.py with a 5th rule (formal-register-in-de)

findings.title: French defaults to formal 'vous', breaking the same warmth rationale that locked German and Italian to informal, with no decision ever recorded
findings.principle: Every locale that ships a consumer-facing register choice states it explicitly in the section-20 locked-decisions table by name (e.g. 'French tu not vous' or 'French vous not tu, because X'), with the same one-line audience-research justification format used for German. A locale's register may not simply default to whatever the translator's habit was; it is a named, owner-approved decision like every other row in that table.
findings.why: SOURCE.md section 18 frames the informal register as a deliberate warmth/distance choice ('per audience research... signals distance in Swiss German consumer contexts', echoed in RATIONALE.md line 524: 'informal address reads warmer and faster; formality signals distance'). If that reasoning is sound for German, the default assumption should be that it also applies to French and Italian consumer products in Switzerland, yet the corpus shows Italian independently converged on informal (matching German) while French converged on formal, meaning either the French translator made an uninstructed register call that contradicts the stated brand voice, or there is a real, undocumented reason French should differ (French 'tu' can read more presumptuous to a French-Swiss audience than German 'du' does to a German-Swiss one) that nobody has actually decided or written down either way.
findings.local_evidence: Programmatic regex scan of messages/fr.json: formal tokens (votre/vos) = 187 raw matches, 229 when measured per-string across the flattened tree; informal tokens (ton/ta/tes/tu/toi) = 46 total (14+3+9+13+7). The formal register appears in core marketing/home surfaces, not just legal copy: home.hero_title 'Votre salon a Bale', home.hero.headlineWord1 'VOTRE PROCHAIN', home.hero.subtitle '...reservez maintenant dans votre ville', home.partner.subtitle 'Faites passer votre entreprise au niveau superieur'. By contrast messages/it.json shows 245 informal (tuo/tua/tuoi/tue) vs 1 formal (Suo family), i.e. Italian independently chose the SAME informal direction as German (245:1 vs de's 196:12), leaving French as the sole outlier (46:229, the inverse ratio) among the three non-English locales.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rni "vous\b\|tutoiement\|vouvoiement\|register.*french\|voice.*french\|register.*italian\|voice.*italian" _design-system/SOURCE.md _design-system/RATIONALE.md _design-system/LOCKFILE.md CLAUDE.md _rules -> zero hits. The section-20 locked-decisions table has one register row ('German du not Sie') and no French or Italian equivalent row.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the WARMTH RATIONALE exists (RATIONALE.md:524) and the German decision exists (SOURCE.md section18/20), but neither one extends the ruling, or even poses the question, for French or Italian. The delta is a missing decision, not a missing rationale.
findings.enforcement: checklist (owner decision needed first), then gate: extend copy-lint-gate.py or a per-locale variant once the FR/IT calls are made

findings.title: ICU plural messages are the documented pattern but at least 9 live customer-facing files hardcode a binary ternary instead, shipping untranslated English or German text to all four locales
findings.principle: No component may render a hardcoded singular/plural string literal (`x === 1 ? "A" : "B"`) for any count the user sees. Every countable UI string routes through next-intl's `{count, plural, one {...} other {...}}` (or the `=1` exact-match form already used elsewhere in this codebase) so the plural form and the word itself both come from the active locale's message file. A PreToolUse/pre-commit grep for the pattern `=== 1 ? "` (or `== 1 ? "`) immediately preceding a JSX text node blocks the edit.
findings.why: A hardcoded ternary bypasses next-intl entirely, so the string is frozen in whatever language the author typed it in (English or German) regardless of which of the four locales the visitor is using; the plural-vs-singular grammar rule (German/French/Italian/English all differ at higher counts, e.g. French treats 0 as singular) is also lost since the ternary only ever tests `=== 1`.
findings.local_evidence: grep -rn '=== 1 ? "' app lib components found 18 raw matches; filtering to genuinely hardcoded user-facing count text (excluding unrelated ternaries like state-machine branches) leaves at least 9 shipped, non-/dev/ files: app/[locale]/brand/[slug]/page.tsx:85 ('Standort'/'Standorte', hardcoded German on a customer brand page), app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonReviews.tsx:142 ('Bewertung'/'Bewertungen'), app/[locale]/_components/profile/FavoritesList.tsx:98 ('Salon'/'Salons'), app/[locale]/_components/search/SalonResultCard.tsx:158 and MapSalonDetail.tsx:57 ('1 Std.' vs '{h} Std.', the canonical card component referenced by LOCKFILE's card grammar), app/[locale]/queue/[token]/page.tsx:242 ('Stern'/'Sterne'), app/[locale]/behandlungen/[...slug]/page.tsx:175 and TreatmentsClient.tsx:176 ('Salon'/'Salons gefunden' on the customer treatment-search page), and app/api/notify/review-posted/route.ts:46 ('1 Stern'/'{rating} Sternen' baked into an outbound notification). By contrast the message files DO contain 10 correct ICU plural keys per locale (e.g. de.json:4992 'salonsAvailable': '{count, plural, =1 {1 Salon} other {# Salons}} verfugbar'), proving the correct pattern is known and used elsewhere, just not consistently.
findings.absence_proof: SOURCE.md section 17.4 documents the correct ICU pattern explicitly ('German has plural forms different from English. Use next-intl plural handling'), so the PRINCIPLE is stated; grep -rn "plural.*gate\|hardcoded.*plural\|ternary.*i18n" ~/.claude/hooks _design-system _rules -> zero hits, confirming there is no enforcement mechanism for the documented rule.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: SOURCE.md section 17.4 states the correct pattern with a code example. It does not name the failure mode (a raw JS ternary substituting for the ICU message) or provide any check for it, and rule 33b's claim that 'untranslated strings should fail the build or trigger a linter warning' is not backed by an actual lint rule (eslint.config.mjs only extends next/core-web-vitals and next/typescript, no i18n plugin).
findings.where_it_should_live: eslint.config.mjs (a custom rule or eslint-plugin-i18next no-literal-string) or ~/.claude/hooks/copy-lint-gate.py as a 6th check
findings.enforcement: gate: literal-plural-ternary check in copy-lint-gate.py, or an ESLint rule wired into the existing lint CI job

findings.title: 112 live call sites hardcode the locale tag 'de-CH' in Intl/toLocaleString calls, a bug the codebase already named and fixed once but never gated
findings.principle: No file may pass a literal BCP-47 locale string ("de-CH", "fr-CH", "it-CH", "en-GB") as an argument to `toLocaleDateString`, `toLocaleTimeString`, `toLocaleString`, or `Intl.NumberFormat`/`Intl.DateTimeFormat` outside of `lib/format.ts` itself. Every other call site must derive the locale from `useLocale()` (or `getLocale()` server-side) and pass it through the shared helpers (`formatDateLabel`, `formatPrice`, `formatCount`) that already do the de/fr/it/en to de-CH/fr-CH/it-CH/en-CH mapping.
findings.why: A French, Italian, or English-browsing user currently sees German date/time formatting (weekday names, month names, and date order) on every one of these 112 call sites regardless of which locale they picked, which is the exact regression `_rules/LESSONS_LEARNED.md` already recorded once as fixed and which a formal audit re-discovered a second time; without a static gate the same fix has to be manually rediscovered a third time once these 112 sites resurface as a complaint.
findings.local_evidence: grep -rn '"de-CH"' app lib components returns 112 current matches, concentrated in the salon-owner dashboard (app/[locale]/dashboard/page.tsx:89-90,141; clients/page.tsx:205,380,419; settings/page.tsx:667,742,1089; calendar/page.tsx:280-857; all-users/page.tsx:235 and more). _rules/LESSONS_LEARNED.md:328-329 already documents this exact bug class from a prior incident ('toLocaleDateString("de-CH") was hardcoded regardless of the user's locale... Fix: Derive localeCode from useLocale()'). _design-system/research/FRONTEND_AUDIT_2026-07-08.md:1238-1239,1367 re-found the identical pattern in 4+ payment/revenue files five weeks after the lesson was written, and named the fix already available in scope (a `locale` variable sitting unused one line above the hardcoded call). lib/format.ts:64-70 already contains the correct SWISS_DATE_LOCALES map (de/en/fr/it -> de-CH/en-CH/fr-CH/it-CH) built for exactly this purpose, so the 112 sites are bypassing an existing, correct utility, not missing one.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn "de-CH.*gate\|hardcoded.locale.*gate\|locale-literal" ~/.claude/hooks _design-system _rules -> zero hits. No ESLint rule (no-restricted-syntax targeting the literal) exists in eslint.config.mjs.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: _rules/LESSONS_LEARNED.md documents the bug and the fix in prose after it happened once; it is retrospective advice, not a rule that prevents recurrence, and the audit trail proves it did recur.
findings.where_it_should_live: eslint.config.mjs (no-restricted-syntax rule banning the literal outside lib/format.ts) or a new PreToolUse hook mirroring copy-lint-gate.py's pattern
findings.enforcement: gate: eslint no-restricted-syntax rule, CI-enforced (fits the existing lint ratchet job in quality.yml)

findings.title: Swiss apostrophe thousands-grouping (1'000) silently does not apply to fr-CH in the ICU data the app actually runs on, and nothing documents or guards the exception
findings.principle: Swiss apostrophe grouping (1'250) is never obtained by passing a mapped Swiss BCP-47 tag (de-CH/fr-CH/it-CH) to Intl.NumberFormat and assuming consistency; `fr-CH` returns space-grouped digits ("1 234 567") in this runtime's ICU data, not apostrophe-grouped ones, while de-CH/it-CH/en-CH all return the apostrophe form. Any number a French-locale user sees (price, count, distance) must either route through a formatter that forces the apostrophe explicitly for all four locales, or the house must accept and document that French numbers legitimately use space-grouping and that is a deliberate, named exception, not an assumption.
findings.why: CLAUDE.md's own probe framing states 'Swiss uses an apostrophe: 1'000' as a flat fact; the code follows the same assumption (mapping fr -> fr-CH expecting Swiss formatting to fall out for free), but the actual runtime disagrees, so the one call site in the codebase that correctly threads a per-locale tag into `formatPrice` (SearchOverlay.tsx:585,667, mapping locale === "fr" -> "fr-CH") produces a price string that reads differently (space vs apostrophe) than every other price on the same page rendered via the de-CH-hardcoded `formatCount` helper, an inconsistency invisible to anyone testing only in German.
findings.local_evidence: Verified via node: `(1234567).toLocaleString('de-CH')` -> "1'234'567", `('it-CH')` -> "1'234'567", `('en-CH')` -> "1'234'567", but `('fr-CH')` -> "1 234 567" and `('fr')` -> "1 234 567" (space, not apostrophe). app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchOverlay.tsx:585 builds `currencyLocale = locale === "fr" ? "fr-CH" : ...` specifically to do 'the right thing' per-locale, then passes it into `formatPrice` at line 667, which will silently space-group for French users while lib/format.ts's `formatCount` (line ~38) hardcodes `.toLocaleString("de-CH")` for every locale, giving apostrophe grouping everywhere else on the same page.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rni "fr-CH.*group\|apostrophe.*fr\|swiss.*grouping.*french\|space.*group" _design-system _rules _docs CLAUDE.md -> zero hits. RATIONALE.md:204 states the Swiss apostrophe convention as a blanket fact ('Swiss thousands grouping... comes free from locale-native formatting') without qualifying that fr-CH is the one locale where this is false.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: RATIONALE.md:204 documents the general Swiss-grouping intent and correctly tells engineers to route through lib/format.ts rather than hand-format; it does not know about, or warn about, the fr-CH exception, so following its own advice (thread the mapped Swiss locale into Intl) produces the wrong visual result for French users.
findings.where_it_should_live: lib/format.ts (fix formatPrice/any number formatter to force apostrophe grouping for all four locales, e.g. post-process the Intl output or use a fixed 'de-CH' grouping source with the correct decimal/currency symbol per locale) + a note in _design-system/RATIONALE.md:204
findings.enforcement: gate: a unit test asserting formatPrice(1234, locale) contains an apostrophe for all four locales, wired into the existing unit-test CI job

findings.title: No CI check for translation-key parity across the four locale files; a missing key currently renders the raw dotted key path to the customer
findings.principle: Every pull request that touches any file under messages/ runs a key-parity check comparing the full flattened key set of de.json (the source of truth locale) against en.json, fr.json, and it.json; any key present in one and missing in another fails CI by name (the exact dotted path), not just a count. Additionally, `i18n.ts`'s getRequestConfig sets an explicit `onError`/`getMessageFallback` that logs the missing key server-side (so it is caught in monitoring) and falls back to the German (default locale) string content instead of next-intl's default behavior of rendering the bare key path to the visitor.
findings.why: next-intl v3's documented default behavior (unconfigured here) is to call console.error and render the dotted namespace.key path as the visible fallback text when a message is missing at request time; with zero onError/getMessageFallback override and zero CI parity check, a translator or a merge that adds a German-only key ships silently and the first evidence anyone gets is a French or Italian visitor seeing literal text like 'onboarding.services.aiSuggestions' on a live screen.
findings.local_evidence: Programmatic key-set diff (flattened, all 4 locales) against de.json as source of truth: en.json is missing 11 keys de.json has (e.g. salon.new, salon.addToFavorites, salon.noAvailability, salon.nextAvailable, salon.removeFromFavorites, salon.appointmentsToday, salon.topSalon, salon.availableToday, salon.partOfBrand, plus refundFlow._todo_translate itself); fr.json is missing 18 (e.g. onboarding.profile.categories, onboarding.profile.atLeastOneCategory, onboarding.hours.addBreak, onboarding.team.nameLabel, dashboard.nav.gallery, onboarding.services.aiSuggestions); it.json is missing 29 (a superset-ish list including onboarding.team.nameLabel, onboarding.hours.removeBreak, reviews.reviewCount, salon.solenTopPick). i18n.ts (read in full) contains no onError or getMessageFallback override at all. No .github/workflows/*.yml or package.json script runs a locale-key diff; grep of scripts/check-invariants.mjs for locale/i18n/messages/ returns nothing.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rni "key parity\|missing.key\|onError\|getMessageFallback\|translation.complet" _design-system _rules _docs CLAUDE.md i18n.ts -> zero hits outside this investigation's own greps.
findings.existing_coverage: none. scripts/audit-i18n.js (see finding copy-i18n-08) checks for hardcoded strings, a related but different failure mode; it never diffs the four JSON files against each other.
findings.where_it_should_live: new scripts/check-i18n-parity.mjs wired into .github/workflows/quality.yml as a fourth job, plus an onError/getMessageFallback addition to i18n.ts
findings.enforcement: gate: ci-i18n-parity job (blocks merge) + a runtime fallback change (behavioral, not a gate)

findings.title: The existing hardcoded-string audit script is unwired, always exits 0, and is too narrow to have caught any of the violations found in this pass
findings.principle: scripts/audit-i18n.js (or its successor) is wired into `npm run lint` or a dedicated CI job, exits non-zero on any new violation versus a checked-in baseline count (the same ratchet pattern already used for tsc and eslint in quality.yml), and its keyword list is replaced by a structural check: any JSX text node or string literal passed directly to a DOM/React text position that is not the argument of `t(...)`, `useTranslations`, or `getTranslations`, and is not inside app/[locale]/dev/**, is a violation, regardless of which language it happens to be written in.
findings.why: A tool that runs manually, never fails the build, and only recognizes 24 specific German words cannot catch English hardcodes (e.g. the 'service'/'services', 'review'/'reviews' literals found in copy-i18n-04), and its keyword-substring matching is so noisy (2213 hits, mostly route strings and CSS-selector-like matches such as 'salon' inside `.from("salons")`) that no one could realistically triage its output, which is presumably why it has never been wired to anything and has sat unused.
findings.local_evidence: scripts/audit-i18n.js:139-141 contains the literal comment '// Don't fail the build, just warn' before `process.exit(0)` unconditionally. grep -n "audit-i18n" package.json .github/workflows/*.yml returns zero matches, i.e. it is not invoked anywhere in the build or CI pipeline. Running it live (`node scripts/audit-i18n.js`) on the current tree returns 2213 violations, the overwhelming majority false positives from route-string and Supabase table-name matches (e.g. app/sitemap.ts:46 flagged for `.from("salons")`), which would make a real signal impossible to see even if someone did run it manually.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n "audit-i18n\|check-i18n\|i18n.*lint" package.json .github/workflows/*.yml -> zero hits confirming it is orphaned tooling.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the SCRIPT exists and demonstrates the intent (rule 33b: 'untranslated strings should fail the build or trigger a linter warning') but delivers neither outcome in its current form.
findings.where_it_should_live: package.json scripts + .github/workflows/quality.yml (new job, ratchet-baseline pattern matching the existing lint job)
findings.enforcement: gate: wire into CI with a ratchet baseline, OR replace with an ESLint rule (see copy-i18n-04) and delete the dead script

findings.title: Copy-length-variance law covers German-vs-English fixed-width containers but not French, and not fixed-HEIGHT single-line buttons
findings.principle: Rule 35's fluid-container mandate extends explicitly to French, not only German: any UI-string container sized for English must tolerate the longer of the German or French translation, since both commonly run 15-35% longer than English depending on string length (a well-known localization-engineering range, see W3C Internationalization guidance on text expansion; no single fixed percentage is claimed here). Additionally, any single-line, fixed-height control (the locked `h-11` button/pill/icon-button row in the design contract) must be verified, per translated string, to not wrap or clip: either the button grows to two lines gracefully by design, or the string is measured against the button's max width in all four locales before the key ships.
findings.why: Rule 35 was written in response to a documented incident (I18N_ROUTING.md's own framing note: '90% of the UI remained in German... layouts broke because German words are longer than English words') but only names German; French is not a rare edge case here, since messages/fr.json alone has 5669 leaf strings running through the same fixed-height button/pill/chip components that rule 35 was written to protect, and the design contract locks button/icon-button height (h-11, 44px) without stating what happens when a translated label is longer than the English or German original.
findings.local_evidence: _rules/I18N_ROUTING.md Rule 35 text names German 3 times and English once, never French or Italian. The design contract table in CLAUDE.md locks 'icon-button: h-11 w-11' and 'CTA... never <=13 on a button' as fixed values with no accompanying overflow/wrap rule for the button row specifically (the 'wrap' row in the same table only covers name/meta/title/body/price in CARDS, not buttons). No script or test in the repo measures rendered button width per locale (grep of scripts/ and package.json for 'measure.*locale\|width.*locale' returns nothing).
findings.existing_coverage: partial: I18N_ROUTING.md Rule 35 states the general fluid-container principle and its German-specific rationale; the delta is (a) it never names French even though French strings run through the same components, and (b) it does not address the one layout shape (fixed-height single-line buttons) that fluid width cannot fix by itself.
findings.enforcement: checklist item in the mockup-first / verifier-loop pipeline (rule 9): screenshot each locale's longest CTA string at h-11 before shipping a new button copy key

findings.title: No dashboard/salon-owner surface distinguishes 'Solen speaking to the owner' (locked informal du) from 'a template the owner sends to their own customer' (which should plausibly be formal, business-register), so the two registers collide inside single components
findings.principle: Any translation key whose rendered text is sent BY a salon owner TO their own customer (quick-reply templates, automated booking-confirmation messages, review-reply drafts) is namespaced separately (e.g. under a `customerFacingTemplates.*` or `.msgTemplate` suffix convention) from keys where Solen's own UI chrome is addressing the salon owner. The register for each namespace is decided once, named in the locked-decisions table, and the copy-lint register gate (copy-i18n-02) treats the two namespaces with different allowed-token sets instead of flagging every 'Ihre' in dashboard.* as drift.
findings.why: Right now dashboard.settings.quickReplyDefault1 ('Vielen Dank fur Ihre Nachricht!') sits in the identical JSON namespace and identical component family as dashboard.settings.vatNumberHint ('Deine... Identifikationsnummer'), with no structural signal distinguishing 'text Solen shows the owner' from 'text the owner's customer will read', so a translator or future editor has no way to know which register a given key should carry, and the register-gate proposed in copy-i18n-02 cannot be scoped correctly without this split existing first.
findings.local_evidence: dashboard.settings.quickReplyDefault1/2 and dashboard.messagesPage.quickReplyThanks/quickReplyConfirmed (the exact strings a salon sends to ITS OWN customer, per their key names) sit alongside dashboard.settings.vatNumberHint, dashboard.settings.salonWarnings, dashboard.settings.stripeConnectDesc (Solen-to-owner chrome, correctly informal 'dein/deine') in the same flat `dashboard.settings` and `dashboard.messagesPage` namespaces with no naming convention separating the two audiences.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rni "customer.facing.template\|owner.facing\|audience.namespace\|template.register" _design-system _rules CLAUDE.md -> zero hits; no such namespacing convention exists anywhere in the messages files (verified by inspecting the dashboard.settings and dashboard.messagesPage key lists directly).
findings.existing_coverage: none. This is a structural precondition the register-gate (copy-i18n-02) needs to be scoped correctly; without it, the gate would either wrongly flag legitimate business-formal owner-to-customer templates or wrongly allow further Sie-drift into Solen's own owner-facing chrome.

findings.title: Swiss price-transparency law (Preisbekanntgabeverordnung) is never named as the reason behind the 'ab CHF' pattern, so nothing checks that 'ab' (starting-from) pricing is only used where the service genuinely has variable pricing
findings.principle: The locked 'ab CHF {N}' / '{price} ab CHF' price-line pattern (LOCKFILE lines 377, 798, 919) carries an explicit rule for WHEN 'ab' may prefix a price: only when the underlying service has more than one priced variant (e.g. hair length, added products) such that the lowest variant price is genuinely the entry point; a flat, single-priced service must never be shown with an 'ab' prefix, since Swiss price-display rules (Preisbekanntgabeverordnung, enforced by the Preisuberwacher/SECO) treat a 'from' price as a genuine floor, not a marketing anchor.
findings.why: This is a pre-launch product that will face real Swiss consumer-protection exposure once salons start entering their own prices; 'ab CHF' is currently a purely visual/copy pattern locked for consistency reasons (LOCKFILE), with no validation tying its use to whether the underlying service_categories row actually has price variance, so a salon (or Solen's own onboarding flow) could attach 'ab' to a flat-rate service and create a compliant-looking but legally risky price display with nobody having decided that was intentional.
findings.local_evidence: LOCKFILE.md:377,798 lock the 'ab CHF {N}' display pattern purely as a visual/copy-hierarchy rule ('meta = ... "ab CHF" amounts'); no reference anywhere in _design-system, _rules, or _docs ties this prefix to an underlying data condition (multiple service price tiers) versus applying it uniformly to every priced service card regardless of whether the salon's service_categories entry has one price or several.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rni "preisbekanntgabe\|price surveillance\|preisuberwach\|starting.price.*legal\|ab CHF.*legal\|pbv\b" _design-system _rules _docs CLAUDE.md -> zero hits anywhere in the estate.
findings.existing_coverage: none as a legal/copy rule; the visual pattern itself is locked (LOCKFILE.md) but purely as typography/hierarchy, not as a data-gated legal display rule.
findings.where_it_should_live: _rules/LESSONS_LEARNED.md or a new _rules/LEGAL_COPY.md, cross-referenced from LOCKFILE's ab-CHF rows
findings.enforcement: checklist (data-gate the 'ab' prefix to services with >1 price tier) then a backend validation
